:::{#sol-epe-split-bias}

Insert the average fit:

$$
\ba
\targetfnf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}
&= \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} + \paren{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&& \text{(add and subtract } \avgfitf{\predvar} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Square it:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&= \sqf{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}}
+ 2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \paren{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
+ \sqf{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&& \text{(expand the square of a sum)}
\ea
$$

Take the expectation of each term in turn.

The first term does not depend on $\trainset$:
$\targetfnf{\predvar}$ is a constant,
and $\avgfitf{\predvar}$ has already been averaged over training sets.
The expectation of a constant is that constant:

$$
\ba
\E{\sqf{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}}}
&= \sqf{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(expectation of a constant)} \\
&= \sqf{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \targetfnf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(a number and its negative have the same square)} \\
&= \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
&& \text{(definitions of the average fit and of bias)}
\ea
$$

The cross term vanishes, and this time not by independence
but by the definition of the average fit.
The first factor is a constant, so it comes out of the expectation:

$$
\ba
\E{2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \paren{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
&= 2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \E{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&& \text{(constant factors)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \paren{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
&& \text{(expectation of a difference of a constant and a variable)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \paren{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(definition of the average fit)} \\
&= 2 \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \avgfitf{\predvar}} \cdot 0
&& \text{(} a - a = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(a number times zero)}
\ea
$$

The third term is the expectation of the squared deviation of the prediction from its mean,
which is the
[variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
of the prediction:

$$
\ba
\E{\sqf{\avgfitf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
&= \E{\sqf{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset} - \avgfitf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(a number and its negative have the same square)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset} - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}}
&& \text{(definition of the average fit)} \\
&= \Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&& \text{(definition of variance)}
\ea
$$

Adding the three expectations,

$$
\E{\sqf{\targetfnf{\predvar} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
= \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}} + \Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}.
$$ {#eq-epe-after-bias}

Neither cross term needed the noise to be normal,
and neither assumed anything about the fitting procedure:
$\fitproc$ can be a line, a tree or a neural network.
This split is specific to squared-error loss, the loss of this chapter's examples.

:::
